feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The candidate is iteration 10 (kd 1.6, score 632.9, the best raced design) with kd raised to 1.8 and nothing else changed. The kd trend at fixed geometry and gains is clear: s-bend progress was 0.46 at kd 0.8 (iteration 3), 0.61 at kd 1.0 with sensors at y 0.06 (iteration 7), 0.84 at kd 1.2 (iteration 8), 0.96 at kd 1.4 (iteration 9), and 0.98 at kd 1.6 (iteration 10). The gain per step is shrinking, from about +0.23 to +0.12 to +0.02, so the s-bend is near saturation. Oval steering_oscillation stayed at 0.19 to 0.20 across the range, so no noise penalty has appeared yet. Slalom has been 0/20 in every iteration, with progress flat at 0.14 to 0.16 since kd 1.2, so damping is not what limits it. kd 1.8 has never raced, and it is a further extrapolation on a trend that is already flattening. The unseen track differs from the development tracks, so the gain from 1.6 to 1.8 is small and uncertain, and noise amplification at higher kd is untested. The proven kd 1.6 design is the safer choice for a single scored race on an unseen track. Revise to that exact design. Do not change kp, base_speed, wheel_track, mass or sensor span, because iterations 2, 4, 5 and 6 showed those reduce oval reliability.
requested_changes: Set controller.kd to 1.6 and keep every other field identical to iteration 10 (kp 5.0, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.2, sensor_weights [-1.0, -0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 1.0], line_loss last_direction; geometry wheel_track 0.10, mass 0.6, body_width 0.18, sensors at y 0.06 with x -0.03 to +0.03 and sensor_size 0.012). This is the best raced design (632.9), and kd 1.4 to 1.6 showed the s-bend gain flattening (0.96 to 0.98).

Do not raise kp or base_speed to chase the slalom. Iteration 4 showed kp 5.5 with base_speed 1.05 cut the oval to 13/20, and the slalom has stayed at 0/20 through every kd change, so the slalom needs a separate test that cannot be run before the single final race.
